subject: Kappa private GPU pool: week-by-week capacity & absorption plan
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Janet Stein <janet.stein@acme-data.com>, ACME Ops <ops@acme-data.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Kappa private GPU pool: week-by-week capacity & absorption plan

Team,

Following the run-through with Acme this morning, I attached an actionable, week-by-week plan that maps their Q2 traffic profile to a staged private GPU pool rollout. The attached workbook (kappa_capacity_model_v3.xlsx) contains the math, but summary here so we can align before sending the SLA draft to Acme.

High-level assumptions (from Acme intake):
- Steady-state inference profile: 4k qps at 256-token avg payloads during business hours; 10k qps peak windows (10m bursts) during nightly batch windows.
- P50 latency target: 120ms for text-gen Llama-variants; p95 under 400ms.
- Model: LlamaX-13B quantized path available (BFloat16 fallback on longer tails).
- Data plane: single VPC in us-west-2, per-rack egress capped by customer's fabric at 80 Gbps.

Proposal (week-by-week):
Week 0 (staging): 2 nodes (A100-80GB equiv) running as an isolated canary. Admission cap 1.5k qps, KV-cache prewarm to 60% expected working set.
Week 1 (initial): 6 nodes, target absorbable throughput 6k qps sustained, reserve 15% safety margin for model warming churn.
Week 2 (scale): 12 nodes, sustained headroom to 12k qps; staging-to-prod cutover for customer traffic routing.
Week 3 (peak posture): 18 nodes, burst capacity to 20k qps via temporary admission-burst windows and greedy batching; maintain per-rack egress budget by sharding heavy batches across NICs.

Network & egress notes:
- Each node assumes up to 12 Gbps egress when hot. Our default packing is 6 nodes per top-of-rack (TOR) with 80Gbps uplink; we recommend splitting burst traffic across two TORs if possible.
- Multihomed NAT gateway recommended to prevent single-point congestion during the nightly 10m bursts.

Operational controls:
- Admission policy: soft-throttle at 85% of absorbable qps, hard reject at 95%.
- Model fallback: if p95 > 500ms for two consecutive 5-min buckets, automatically route to a smaller quantized variant (LlamaX-7B-Q) with a 1.8x efficiency gain.
- Warmup choreography: pre-fetch KV entries for top-500 prefixes 10 minutes before scheduled peak windows.

Next actions for internal alignment:
1) Laura: validate staging network VLAN carveouts with Acme infra team and confirm TOR placement (ETA Mon 3/25).
2) Ben: confirm we can provision 18 A100-80 equiv nodes in us-west-2 private pool and estimate lead times for on-prem racks (ETA Tue 3/26).
3) Neha: sanity-check the workbook's cost versus committed capacity model and produce a fallback discount schedule if Acme requests a larger reserved commitment.

I'll hold off on sending the SLA draft until we lock the staging dates and TOR plan. Janet/ACME Ops — if this sequencing looks reasonable on your side, please reply with preferred cutover day and any fabric constraints we missed.

Thanks,
Chloe

--
Chloe Martin

From: Janet Stein <janet.stein@acme-data.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Ops <ops@acme-data.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kappa private GPU pool: week-by-week capacity & absorption plan

Chloe — thanks for the clear plan. A few notes from Acme infra: we have two physical TOR uplinks available in the target rack (both 100Gbps), but they run through different aggregation switches with slightly different latencies (approx +0.6ms on path B).

Questions/requests:
- Can you confirm whether the admission soft-throttle will impact long-polling streaming sessions (we have a small subset that keeps connections open for up to 30s)?
- For the KV prefetch, can we provide the top-500 prefixes as a csv interface or do you want us to push a redis snapshot?
- We prefer the cutover on Thu 4/4 evening PST to align with our maintenance window.

If you can answer the above by Monday, we'll lock the maintenance window.

—Janet
VP, Platform Engineering, Acme Data
janet.stein@acme-data.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Janet Stein <janet.stein@acme-data.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Mar 2029 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kappa private GPU pool: week-by-week capacity & absorption plan

Chloe/Team — quick readout after talking to infra sourcing and the field ops team:
- Hardware availability: us-west-2 regional pool has 24 A100-80 equiv nodes available for Dedicated reservations; lead time for physical on-prem rack installs (if Acme wants us to ship appliances) is ~6 weeks from PO. Provisioning into their VPC private pool (partner-hosted blades) is possible within 10 business days once we have TOR mapping.
- Egress mitigation: we can enable NIC-level egress shaping per node; suggestion is to cap node bursts to 10 Gbps during nightly windows and rely on ingress-spread to avoid TOR oversubscription.
- Streaming sessions: soft-throttle will only apply to admission at request entry; established streaming sessions will be allowed to drain but will be subject to adaptive packet shaping to preserve latency SLOs. In short: no forced mid-stream disconnects, but we will reduce throughput to keep p95 in range.

I'll push the exact provisioning timeline into INF-9123 and attach a sample PO template.

—Ben
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Janet Stein <janet.stein@acme-data.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Mar 2029 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kappa private GPU pool: week-by-week capacity & absorption plan

Thanks everyone — inline answers and next steps: 

Janet: soft-throttle behavior — confirmed by Ben, streaming sessions won't be abruptly closed. We'll add a short paragraph to the SLA noting adaptive shaping for open streams and a 5-minute ramp window to avoid client-side retry storms. For KV prefetch we support both CSV list and redis snapshot; CSV is easiest for us to ingest into the warmup job, but we'll take the snapshot if Acme prefers.

Operations notes to internal team:
- Laura: please schedule a 30-min TOR alignment call with Acme Ops (ops@acme-data.com) before Thu 3/28. We need the wiring diagram and VLAN IDs to validate the recommended dual-TOR placement.
- Ben: confirm the on-prem appliance SKU and include the NIC shaping config in the PO (cap bursts to 10 Gbps, explicit per-node egress ceiling).
- Neha: I'll need the fallback pricing band by EOD Wed 3/27 so we can present a committed-capacity option during the cutover planning meeting.

I'll update the SLA-draft (attached) and circulate once TOR confirmation is in.

Chloe
